cases.prompt: Review the staged change described in the input file and give me your review with a merge recommendation. Do not run any commands; everything you need is in the input file.
expected_behavior: Uses the interactive report: a Review heading, a Verdict line, a Depth line with its reason, Blocking and Follow-up findings, Proofs, Claims checked
Verdict is changes-required because of the SQL injection and the never-matching usage increment
Findings cite file plus function, not line numbers
Names mutants the weak tests would let survive, marks unrun proofs as not run, and audits the 14-tests and expiry-covered claims against the log
Does not ask for new result types against the plain-dict convention

assertions.name: reviewer-quality
rubric: The f-string SQL in apply_discount is reported as a critical injection issue with a fix that uses the project's %s placeholder convention
The review notes that the UPDATE uses the un-normalised code, so lowercase input never increments uses, and that the cap check allows one use past max_uses
The review contrasts the author's 'All 14 tests pass' and 'expiry is fully covered' claims with the log showing 13 passed and the expiry test skipped
The review states which mutants (for example wrong discount math or a >= cap) the existing assertions would not catch, and proposes assertions that would

cases.prompt: An orchestrator agent has delegated the code review described in the input file to you. Write the report you would return to it. Do not run any commands; everything you need is in the input file.
expected_behavior: Returns the delegated report: a verdict line bound to head 3f9a2c1d, a Depth line, Blocking, Follow-up, Mutants, Claims checked, Not verified, Outside this PR, Long form
Verdict is changes-required or close: the helper swallows every timeout and the failed-jobs assertion was removed
Severity is rated on the findings, not lowered because this is round 3
The root cause and the 50-run and CI-green claims are marked unproven or refuted; the report has no markdown headings

assertions.name: reviewer-quality
rubric: The report identifies that waitForDrain swallows the final timeout, so the test passes even when the queue never drains, and rates it blocking
The removed expect(queue.failed) assertion is reported as lost coverage, and severity is not lowered because this is round 3
The '0 failures in 50 runs' claim and the CI run on main@b71e0a4 (before PR #409 touched src/retryQueue.ts) are marked unverified or refuted
The report does not claim any mutant or probe was actually run; unrun proofs appear under Not verified

cases.prompt: Review the pull request described in the input file and give me your review with a merge verdict. Do not run any commands; everything you need is in the input file.
expected_behavior: The review is sized by blast radius, not by the clean-looking code or the teammate's LGTM, because the partner generates clients from this contract and ships next week
The verdict is changes-required, with the contract's shape as a blocking finding despite green tests, full coverage and the versioned path

It names the subtle costly shapes: a closed status enum that Billing's planned statuses will break in generated clients, an orders response that is a bare array and so cannot gain paging metadata, page offsets over a list that grows at the top, timestamps without an offset despite format date-time, and order totals without their currency
With no REVIEW.md in the repository, it ends with a Scope brief proposing one that lists the partner routes and their OpenAPI document as expensive to change

assertions.name: reviewer-quality
rubric: The review sizes the change by blast radius: the partner generates Swift and Kotlin clients from this contract and old app versions stay installed for months, so 'read-only, versioned, tests green' does not make it low risk

It finds that the closed status enum, with no unknown value, breaks decoding in the partner's generated clients once Billing adds trial and past_due, and that the STATUS map then yields no status at all

It finds that the orders response is a bare top-level array, so paging metadata such as a cursor or has-more flag cannot be added later without a breaking change, and that page offsets skip or repeat orders as new ones arrive
It finds that the timestamps carry no offset although the contract says date-time, and that order totals omit their currency although orders have one
These contract issues are blocking and the verdict is changes-required; it does not invent problems the change has solved, such as a missing version or leaked database keys

cases.prompt: Review the branch described in the input file and give me your review with a merge recommendation. Do not run any commands; everything you need is in the input file.
expected_behavior: Applies the repository's REVIEW.md: the float64 conversion in money breaks its Always check rule and is blocking; the verdict is changes-required
Treats the CSV header and columns as a surface others build on, though neither the generic examples nor the brief list it

Ends with a Scope brief proposal, separate from this branch: add the CSV export under Expensive to change, fix the internal/report/json.go entry that #240 moved to internal/render, and revisit the brief in full because its Revisited date is more than three months old

assertions.name: brief-revisit-due
assertions.pattern: (?s)Scope brief\b.{0,800}?(?i:2026-03-02|three months|3 months|seven months|7 months|in full|full revisit)

assertions.name: scope-quality
rubric: The float64 conversion in money is a blocking finding grounded in REVIEW.md's Always check rule, with a decimal-based fix such as StringFixed(2)
The CSV header names and column order are treated as a contract the accountants' bank imports map by name, not as an internal detail
The review proposes REVIEW.md edits as a change separate from this branch: list the CSV export as expensive to change, and replace the stale internal/report/json.go entry
It notes the brief was last revisited 2026-03-02, more than three months ago, and recommends revisiting it in full
It does not fold the REVIEW.md edit into the branch under review
